title: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

blocks.tex: We work with the fixed classical and synthetic categories, their Adams systems, and their chosen object families. Classical spectra in \cite{LWX126} are 2-completed, connective, and of finite type. The statements below concern classical input, synthetic comparison theorems, and secondary operations. Paper numbering refers to \cite{LWX126}; see the \href{paper/2412.10879.pdf}{original paper}.

blocks.title: Classical input and realization

blocks.label: sem:Literature:connected-homology
blocks.title: Connectivity and mod-two homology
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{SchwedeSymmetricSpectra}, Prop. II.5.22; \cite{EKMM}, Thm. IV.4.5.)\par{}

The sphere is $(-1)$-connected. If $X$ is $n$-connected, then $H_i(X;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $i\le n$. There is an additive universal-coefficient equivalence
\[H^n(X;\mathbb F_2)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H_{-n}(X;\mathbb F_2),\mathbb F_2).\]
Both groups use the same classical category and coefficient object.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.connected_homology_vanishing
lean.code:
public theorem connected_homology_vanishing :
  ∀ (X : Spectrum) (n : ℤ), IsConnected X n →
    ∀ i : ℤ, i ≤ n → Subsingleton (ModTwoHomology model.coefficients i X) := by
  sorry

blocks.label: sem:Literature:realization-coordinates
blocks.title: Realization in sphere coordinates
blocks.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40.)\par{}

Let $\operatorname{Re}$ be the additive realization functor with sphere isomorphisms $S^m\cong\operatorname{Re}(S^{m,w})$. Its isomorphism at the unit is the $\nu$--realization comparison. In these coordinates, realization sends each sphere map $\lambda^k$ to the identity. Write $\operatorname{Re}(a)$ for the induced realization of a sphere class or a class on $\nu X$.

        (realization_sphere m w).hom := by

blocks.label: sem:Literature:hopf-classes
blocks.title: The Hopf classes and their synthetic normalization
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams58}, Lem. 2.3; \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.16.)\par{}

The classical maps $\eta$ and $\nu$ are detected by the nonzero permanent cycles $h_1\in E_2^{1,2}$ and $h_2\in E_2^{1,4}$, respectively. The normalized synthetic lift $\eta\in\pi_{1,2}S^{0,0}$ has filtration exponent one, first-quotient label $h_1$, and realization equal to the classical $\eta$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.eta_exponent
lean.code:
public theorem eta_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap = 1 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨_, _, b, hb, _⟩ := eta_detection
  have hmem : model.auxiliary.etaMap ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _
      ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 1) := by
    change ∃ b, ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 1).arrow.hom b = _
    exact ⟨b, hb⟩
  simp only [AbstractAdamsTower.filtration, OrderIso.apply_symm_apply] at hmem
  obtain ⟨lift, hlift⟩ := hmem
  have hF : MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap 1 :=
    ⟨lift, hlift⟩
  change (if MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap 1 then 1 else 0) = 1
  exact if_pos hF
lean.statement:
public theorem eta_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.etaMap = 1

Scope of the related interface family `literature-classical`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 共享经典来源、θ₅/Hopf检测、实际realization及HF₂基础结果；任意synthetic θ₅选择输运仍是独立证明责任。

- **constraints**: stem62_exponent_two applies only to the same ordinary sphere element a satisfying ∃ n : ℕ, (2^n : ℕ) • a = 0. No unconditional ordinary 62-stem exponent-two assertion is provided. Selected theta5 order-two proof and Main arbitrary-choice repairs remain explicit integration blockers; no new pending obligation is authorized.

Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The classical detections and nonzero permanence are ordinary Hopf facts. The normalized synthetic map is the project chosen lift with exponent e(eta)=1, not a literal named theorem in Adams60. Realization uses the specified nu-unit and lambda-inverting comparison. This verifies the mathematical source and the stated adaptation, not the pending comparison with the fixed project model. No Lean proof obligation is discharged by this audit. Primary references: [Adams58](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Adams-SS.pdf): Lemma 2.3 and the following m=0 paragraph; pages 184 [Adams60](https://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/adams1.pdf): Section 1.1, after Theorem 1.1.1; pages 20 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Proposition 3.16; Notation 3.19; Notation 7.2; pages [18, 19, 42] [Pst](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.01804v3): Proposition 4.40 and Remark 4.41; pages 49

blocks.label: sem:Literature:theta-five
blocks.title: A detected Kervaire class in stem 62
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BJMtheta5}, Thm. 2.1; \cite{Xu}, Cor. 1.3.)\par{}

There is a classical class $\theta_5\in\pi_{62}S^0$ of order two detected by the nonzero permanent cycle $h_5^2\in E_2^{2,64}$. Fix such a class. There is a synthetic lift $a\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ with first-quotient label $h_5^2$ and $\operatorname{Re}(a)=\theta_5$.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:theta-indeterminacy
blocks.title: The 2-primary stem and the filtration of choices
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{IWX}, Table 1; \cite{LWX126}, proof of Lem. 7.10.)\par{}

Every class $a\in\pi_{62}S^0$ annihilated by a power of two satisfies $2a=0$. If $a,b\in\pi_{62}S^0$ are detected by $h_5^2$, then $a-b$ has Adams filtration at least six.

  ∀ a : HomotopyGroup (C := Spectrum) 62 SphereSpectrum,
    (∃ n : ℕ, (2 ^ n : ℕ) • a = 0) → a + a = 0 := by
  sorry
lean.docstring:
The ordinary 62-stem has exponent two on its 2-primary subgroup.
Odd-primary summands are not covered by this source obligation.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:tmf-convergence
blocks.title: Connectivity, finite type, and convergence for tmf
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, §1.2.)\par{}

The spectrum $\mathit{tmf}$ is connective and has finite mod-two homology in each degree. Its classical Adams tower converges to its homotopy groups with their Adams filtration. Transport along $\mathit{tmf}\cong D$ preserves tower lifts and associated-graded representatives.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.tmf_convergence
lean.code:
public def tmf_convergence :
  ClassicalTowerConvergence model.classicalTower tmf := by
  let e : tmf ≅ model.auxiliary.detector := tmfIso
  let c : ClassicalTowerConvergence model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.detector :=
    model.classicalConvergence .detector
  have tmf_filtration_map {X Y : Spectrum} (f : X ⟶ Y) (s m : ℤ) (x : HomotopyGroup m X)
      (hx : x ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower X).filtrationSubmodule s m) :
      x ≫ f ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtrationSubmodule s m := by
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hx
    refine ⟨a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map f).stage s.toNat, ?_⟩
    change (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map f).stage s.toNat) ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).projection s =
      (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower X).projection s) ≫ f
    rw [Category.assoc, (model.classicalTower.map f).projection s, ← Category.assoc]

  have tmf_filtration_iso_mem {X Y : Spectrum} (e : X ≅ Y) (s m : ℤ)
      (x : AbstractAdamsTower.homotopy X m) :
      x ≫ e.hom ∈
          ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtration.F s m) ↔
        x ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((model.classicalTower.tower X).filtration.F s m) := by
    simp (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [AbstractAdamsTower.filtration, OrderIso.apply_symm_apply]
    change x ≫ e.hom ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtrationSubmodule s m ↔
      x ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower X).filtrationSubmodule s m
    constructor
    · intro hx
      simpa (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [Category.assoc, e.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id] using
        tmf_filtration_map e.inv s m (x ≫ e.hom) hx
    · exact tmf_filtration_map e.hom s m x

  have tmf_quotient_iso {R : Type} [Ring R] {M N : ModuleCat.{0} R}
      (B Z : Subobject M) (B' Z' : Subobject N) (h : B ≤ Z) (h' : B' ≤ Z')
      (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N)
      (hB : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) B' ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) B)
      (hZ : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) Z' ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) Z) :
      ∃ q : cokernel (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) ≅ cokernel (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h'),
        ∀ a : (Subobject.underlying.obj Z : ModuleCat R),
          ∃ b : (Subobject.underlying.obj Z' : ModuleCat R),
            Z'.arrow b = e (Z.arrow a) ∧
            q.hom (cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) a) =
              cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h') b := by
    have restrict (S : Subobject M) (T : Subobject N)
        (he : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S) :
        ∃ w : Subobject.underlying.obj S ≅ Subobject.underlying.obj T,
          ∀ a, T.arrow (w.hom a) = e (S.arrow a) := by
      let a := LinearEquiv.ofInjective S.arrow.hom ((ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).mp inferInstance)
      let b := LinearEquiv.ofInjective T.arrow.hom ((ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).mp inferInstance)
      have hm : ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S).map e.toLinearMap =
          (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T := by
        ext y
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          exact (he x).2 hx
        · intro hy
          refine ⟨e.symm y, (he (e.symm y)).1 ?_, e.apply_symm_apply y⟩
          simpa (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [e.apply_symm_apply] using hy
      let c := e.ofSubmodules ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S) ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T) hm
      refine ⟨((a.trans c).trans b.symm).toModuleIso, ?_⟩
      intro x
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (b.apply_symm_apply (c (a x)))
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := restrict B B' hB
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := restrict Z Z' hZ
  -- … (truncated)

public def tmf_convergence :
  ClassicalTowerConvergence model.classicalTower tmf := by
  let e : tmf ≅ model.auxiliary.detector := tmfIso
  let c : ClassicalTowerConvergence model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.detector :=
    model.classicalConvergence .detector
  have tmf_filtration_map {X Y : Spectrum} (f : X ⟶ Y) (s m : ℤ) (x : HomotopyGroup m X)
      (hx : x ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower X).filtrationSubmodule s m) :
      x ≫ f ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtrationSubmodule s m := by
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hx
    refine ⟨a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map f).stage s.toNat, ?_⟩
    change (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map f).stage s.toNat) ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).projection s =
      (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower X).projection s) ≫ f
    rw [Category.assoc, (model.classicalTower.map f).projection s, ← Category.assoc]

  have tmf_filtration_iso_mem {X Y : Spectrum} (e : X ≅ Y) (s m : ℤ)
      (x : AbstractAdamsTower.homotopy X m) :
      x ≫ e.hom ∈
          ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtration.F s m) ↔
        x ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _ ((model.classicalTower.tower X).filtration.F s m) := by
    simp (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [AbstractAdamsTower.filtration, OrderIso.apply_symm_apply]
    change x ≫ e.hom ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower Y).filtrationSubmodule s m ↔
      x ∈ (model.classicalTower.tower X).filtrationSubmodule s m
    constructor
    · intro hx
      simpa (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [Category.assoc, e.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id] using
        tmf_filtration_map e.inv s m (x ≫ e.hom) hx
    · exact tmf_filtration_map e.hom s m x

  have tmf_quotient_iso {R : Type} [Ring R] {M N : ModuleCat.{0} R}
      (B Z : Subobject M) (B' Z' : Subobject N) (h : B ≤ Z) (h' : B' ≤ Z')
      (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N)
      (hB : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) B' ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) B)
      (hZ : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) Z' ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) Z) :
      ∃ q : cokernel (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) ≅ cokernel (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h'),
        ∀ a : (Subobject.underlying.obj Z : ModuleCat R),
          ∃ b : (Subobject.underlying.obj Z' : ModuleCat R),
            Z'.arrow b = e (Z.arrow a) ∧
            q.hom (cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) a) =
              cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h') b := by
    have restrict (S : Subobject M) (T : Subobject N)
        (he : ∀ x, e x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T ↔ x ∈ (ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S) :
        ∃ w : Subobject.underlying.obj S ≅ Subobject.underlying.obj T,
          ∀ a, T.arrow (w.hom a) = e (S.arrow a) := by
      let a := LinearEquiv.ofInjective S.arrow.hom ((ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).mp inferInstance)
      let b := LinearEquiv.ofInjective T.arrow.hom ((ModuleCat.mono_iff_injective _).mp inferInstance)
      have hm : ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S).map e.toLinearMap =
          (ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T := by
        ext y
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
          exact (he x).2 hx
        · intro hy
          refine ⟨e.symm y, (he (e.symm y)).1 ?_, e.apply_symm_apply y⟩
          simpa (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [e.apply_symm_apply] using hy
      let c := e.ofSubmodules ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule M) S) ((ModuleCat.subobjectModule N) T) hm
      refine ⟨((a.trans c).trans b.symm).toModuleIso, ?_⟩
      intro x
      exact congrArg Subtype.val (b.apply_symm_apply (c (a x)))
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := restrict B B' hB
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := restrict Z Z' hZ
    have comm : Subobject.ofLE B Z h ≫ z.hom = b.hom ≫ Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h' := by
      apply (cancel_mono Z'.arrow).1
      apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro x
      change Z'.arrow (z.hom (Subobject.ofLE B Z h x)) =
        Z'.arrow (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h' (b.hom x))
      rw [hz]
      have hs := congrArg (fun f => f.hom x) (Subobject.ofLE_arrow h)
      have ht := congrArg (fun f => f.hom (b.hom x)) (Subobject.ofLE_arrow h')
      change Z.arrow (Subobject.ofLE B Z h x) = B.arrow x at hs
      change Z'.arrow (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h' (b.hom x)) = B'.arrow (b.hom x) at ht
      rw [hs, ht, hb]
    let q := cokernel.mapIso (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h') b z comm
    refine ⟨q, fun a => ⟨z.hom a, hz a, ?_⟩⟩
    have hq : cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B Z h) ≫ q.hom =
        z.hom ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B' Z' h') := by
      simp (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [q, cokernel.mapIso_hom, cokernel.map, cokernel.π_desc]
    exact congrArg (fun f => f.hom a) hq
  let homotopyIso (m : ℤ) :
      AbstractAdamsTower.homotopy tmf m ≅ AbstractAdamsTower.homotopy model.auxiliary.detector m := {
    hom := ModuleCat.ofHom (inducedMap e.hom m).toIntLinearMap
    inv := ModuleCat.ofHom (inducedMap e.inv m).toIntLinearMap
    hom_inv_id := by
      ext a
      change (a ≫ e.hom) ≫ e.inv = a
      simp (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [Category.assoc, e.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
    inv_hom_id := by
      ext a
      change (a ≫ e.inv) ≫ e.hom = a
      simp (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [Category.assoc, e.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id] }
  let infinityIso (p : ℤ × ℤ) :
      ((model.classical.obj tmf).ssData p).eInfty ≅ ((model.classical.obj model.auxiliary.detector).ssData p).eInfty := {
    hom := (model.classical.map e.hom).eInftyMap p
    inv := (model.classical.map e.inv).eInftyMap p
    hom_inv_id := by
      rw [← SpectralSequenceMorphism.eInftyMap_comp, ← model.classical.map_comp, e.hom_inv_id,
        model.classical.map_id, SpectralSequenceMorphism.eInftyMap_id]
    inv_hom_id := by
      rw [← SpectralSequenceMorphism.eInftyMap_comp, ← model.classical.map_comp, e.inv_hom_id,
        model.classical.map_id, SpectralSequenceMorphism.eInftyMap_id] }
  have gr (s m : ℤ) :
      ∃ q : (model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.associatedGraded s m ≅
        (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.associatedGraded s m,
        ∀ b : (Subobject.underlying.obj ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.F s m) : ModuleCat ℤ),
          ∃ b' : (Subobject.underlying.obj ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.F s m) : ModuleCat ℤ),
            ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.F s m).arrow b' =
              ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.F s m).arrow b ≫ e.hom ∧
            q.hom ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.toAssociatedGraded s m b) =
              (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.toAssociatedGraded s m b' := by
    exact tmf_quotient_iso
      ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.F (s+1) m) ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.F s m)
      ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.F (s+1) m) ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.F s m)
      ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.mono s m) ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.mono s m)
      (homotopyIso m).toLinearEquiv
      (tmf_filtration_iso_mem e (s+1) m) (tmf_filtration_iso_mem e s m)
  let q := fun s m => (gr s m).choose
  refine ⟨fun p => infinityIso p ≪≫ c.identification p ≪≫ (q p.1 (p.2-p.1)).symm, ?_⟩
  intro p a z hz b hb
  let z' := (model.classical.map e.hom).toSSDataMorphism.cycleMap p ⊤ z
  let a' := a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map e.hom).stage p.1.toNat
  obtain ⟨b', hb', hq⟩ := (gr p.1 (p.2-p.1)).choose_spec b
  have hz' : (model.classicalTower.sequence model.auxiliary.detector).infiniteRepresentativeE1 p z' =
      (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).layerMap p a' := by
    have hc := congrArg (fun f => f.hom z)
      ((model.classical.map e.hom).toSSDataMorphism.cycleMap_arrow p ⊤)
    change (((model.classical.obj model.auxiliary.detector).ssData p).Z ⊤).arrow z' =
      (model.classical.map e.hom).φ p ((((model.classical.obj tmf).ssData p).Z ⊤).arrow z) at hc
    unfold TowerSequencePresentation.infiniteRepresentativeE1
    rw [hc, model.classicalTower.natural]
    change (model.classicalTower.sequence tmf).infiniteRepresentativeE1 p z ≫ (model.classicalTower.map e.hom).layer p.1 =
      (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).layerMap p a'
    rw [hz]
    change (a ≫ HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibι _) ≫ (model.classicalTower.map e.hom).layer p.1 =
      (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map e.hom).stage p.1.toNat) ≫ HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibι _
    dsimp only [TowerMap.layer]
    rw [Category.assoc, ← HasFunctorialCofiber.cofibMap_ι, ← Category.assoc]
  have hb'' : ((model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).filtration.F p.1 (p.2-p.1)).arrow b' =
      a' ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).projection p.1 := by
    rw [hb', hb]
    change (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower tmf).projection p.1) ≫ e.hom =
      (a ≫ (model.classicalTower.map e.hom).stage p.1.toNat) ≫ (model.classicalTower.tower model.auxiliary.detector).projection p.1
    simpa (config := { congrConsts := false }) only [Category.assoc] using
      congrArg (fun f => a ≫ f) ((model.classicalTower.map e.hom).projection p.1).symm
  have hc := c.canonical p a' z' hz' b' hb''
  have hpage := congrArg (fun f => f.hom z)
    ((model.classical.map e.hom).toSSDataMorphism.pageπ_pageMap p ⊤)
  change (model.classical.map e.hom).eInftyMap p (((model.classical.obj tmf).ssData p).pageπ ⊤ z) =
    ((model.classical.obj model.auxiliary.detector).ssData p).pageπ ⊤ z' at hpage
  change (q p.1 (p.2-p.1)).inv
      ((c.identification p).hom
        ((model.classical.map e.hom).eInftyMap p (((model.classical.obj tmf).ssData p).pageπ ⊤ z))) = _
  rw [hpage, hc, ← hq]
  exact congrArg (fun f => f.hom ((model.classicalTower.tower tmf).filtration.toAssociatedGraded p.1 (p.2-p.1) b))
    (q p.1 (p.2-p.1)).hom_inv_id

blocks.title: The class g and the detection of bar-kappa
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, Thm. 11.61(20).)\par{}

The group $E_2^{4,24}(S^0)$ has a unique nonzero element $g$. It detects a class $\bar\kappa\in\pi_{20}S^0$, which we fix.

The group $E_2^{9,54}(S^0)$ has a unique nonzero element $\Delta h_1g$. It detects a class $w\in\pi_{45}S^0$, which we fix.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:nu-page-coordinates
blocks.title: Weight coordinates on the synthetic Adams pages
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family, weight shift induces isomorphisms
\[E_r^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong E_r^{s,t,w-1}(\Sigma^{0,-1}\nu X).\]
For $k\ge0$, the $E_2$ labels in tridegree $(s,t,t-k)$ are the classical labels in bidegree $(s,t)$. Under these coordinates, the map induced by $\lambda:\Sigma^{0,-1}\nu X\to\nu X$ lowers weight by one.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.nuPage_weightShift
lean.code:
public def nuPage_weightShift :
  ∀ (X : ClassicalObject) (r s t w : ℤ),
    (model.family.nu model.nu (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page r (s,t,w) ≅
      (model.family.obj ((SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,-1)).obj
        (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)))).Page r (s,t,w-1) := by
  intro X r s t w
  let two : ℤ := 2
  let F := model.family
  let V := model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)
  let shiftedV := (SyntheticCategory.biShift (0,-1)).obj V
  let shift (page : ℤ) (hp : two ≤ page) :
      (F.obj V).Page page (s,t,w) ≅ (F.obj shiftedV).Page page (s,t,w-1) :=
    let q := t-s
    let q0 := q+0
    let a := q+s
    let b := q0+s
    let addS := fun z : ℤ => z+s
    let hq0 : q0=q := Int.add_zero q
    let hba : b=a := @congrArg ℤ ℤ q0 q addS hq0
    let hat : a=t := Int.sub_add_cancel t s
    let isoAt := fun aa bb : ℤ =>
      (F.obj V).Page page (s,aa,w) ≅ (F.obj shiftedV).Page page (s,bb,w-1)
    let raw : isoAt a b :=
      KIP126.AdamsSynthetic.Standard.shift_page (0,-1) (.nu X) page hp (q,w) s
    let same : isoAt a a := Eq.rec (motive := fun z _ => isoAt a z) raw hba
    Eq.rec (motive := fun z _ => isoAt z z) same hat
  by_cases hr : two ≤ r
  · exact shift r hr
  · let hlt : r < two := @Int.lt_of_not_ge two r hr
    let hle : r ≤ two := @Int.le_of_lt r two hlt
    let htwo : two ≤ two := Int.le_refl two
    let pageIso (Y : SyntheticSpectrum) (p : Tridegree) :
        (F.obj Y).Page r p ≅ (F.obj Y).Page two p :=
      let E := F.obj Y
      let c := E.sequence.r₀
      let hfirst : c=two := SyntheticAdamsFamily.firstPage F Y
      let nR := (r-c).toNat
      let nBase := (r-two).toNat
      let nTwo := (two-c).toNat
      let nZero : ℕ := 0
      let P : Prop := nBase=nZero
      let Q : Prop := r ≤ two
      let hiff : P ↔ Q := Int.toNat_sub_eq_zero_iff r two
      let hBase : P := @Iff.mpr P Q hiff hle
      let indexR := fun z : ℤ => (r-z).toNat
      let indexTwo := fun z : ℤ => (two-z).toNat
      let hR : nR=nBase := @congrArg ℤ ℕ c two indexR hfirst
      let hRZero : nR=nZero := @Eq.trans ℕ nR nBase nZero hR hBase
      let hTwo : nTwo=nZero := @congrArg ℤ ℕ c two indexTwo hfirst
      let A := ModuleCat.{0} ℤ
      let D := E.sequence.ssData p
      let pageN : ℕ → A := fun n => D.page (n : WithTop ℕ)
      let objR := pageN nR
      let objTwo := pageN nTwo
      let objZero := pageN nZero
      let hObjR : objR=objZero := @congrArg ℕ A nR nZero pageN hRZero
      let hObjTwo : objTwo=objZero := @congrArg ℕ A nTwo nZero pageN hTwo
      let hObjTwoSymm : objZero=objTwo := @Eq.symm A objTwo objZero hObjTwo
      let hObj : objR=objTwo := @Eq.trans A objR objZero objTwo hObjR hObjTwoSymm
      eqToIso hObj
  -- … (truncated)

      let nR := (r-c).toNat

      let hBase : P := @Iff.mpr P Q hiff hle
      let indexR := fun z : ℤ => (r-z).toNat
      let indexTwo := fun z : ℤ => (two-z).toNat
      let hR : nR=nBase := @congrArg ℤ ℕ c two indexR hfirst
      let hRZero : nR=nZero := @Eq.trans ℕ nR nBase nZero hR hBase
      let hTwo : nTwo=nZero := @congrArg ℤ ℕ c two indexTwo hfirst
      let A := ModuleCat.{0} ℤ
      let D := E.sequence.ssData p
      let pageN : ℕ → A := fun n => D.page (n : WithTop ℕ)
      let objR := pageN nR
      let objTwo := pageN nTwo
      let objZero := pageN nZero
      let hObjR : objR=objZero := @congrArg ℕ A nR nZero pageN hRZero
      let hObjTwo : objTwo=objZero := @congrArg ℕ A nTwo nZero pageN hTwo

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The public shift isomorphism includes integer pages below 2; those pages are frozen to the first page by a project convention, not covered as extra pages in the cited paper. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). blocks.label: sem:Literature:free-lambda-range
blocks.title: The free-lambda comparison range
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8 and Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $r\ge2$ and $r-2\le t-w$, there is an isomorphism
\[E_r^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong E_r^{s,t}(X).\]
It preserves $E_2$ labels and commutes with $\lambda$ and the differentials. Its inverse gives classical lifts with the same differential and $\lambda$ compatibilities.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. Put a=t-w. In the polynomial-lambda spectral sequence of BHS Theorem A.8, an incoming classical d_i has a source label with lambda exponent a-i+1. All incoming differentials contributing before page r have 2<=i<=r-1, so they all occur once a>=r-2. Outgoing cycles agree under localization. Thus the localization map is an isomorphism for a>=r-2, including the boundary case; this is a derived range, not the literal range printed in Corollary A.9(4). The inverse, E2 normalization, lambda square and differential square are obtained from this same localization map, rather than from unrelated choices of isomorphism. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): paragraph immediately before Notation A.7; proof of Theorem A.8; pages arXiv PDF p. 72; published p. 307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7; pages local PDF p. 16; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Theorem A.8 and Corollary A.9; grading as in [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:lambda-inversion
blocks.title: The comparison obtained by inverting lambda
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40; \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8.)\par{}

Inverting $\lambda$ induces a morphism from the synthetic cycle-and-boundary data of $\nu X$ to the classical data. It preserves cycles, boundaries, and $E_2$ labels, commutes with $d_r$ for $r\ge2$, and carries multiplication by $\lambda$ to the identity. For $r-2\le t-w$, its page map is the preceding free-range isomorphism.

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $q>0$,
\[E_2^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)\cong
\begin{cases}E_2^{s,t}(X),&0\le t-w<q,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
In the displayed strip, the quotient projection preserves labels and is an isomorphism on $E_2$.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The canonical nu-E Adams resolution can be tensored with C-tau^q. Its polynomial E1 terms truncate to exponents 0,...,q-1; the d1 calculation then gives the stated E2 strip. At weight exponent a=t-w, passing to page r inspects outgoing d_i for i<=r-1 whose target exponent is a+i-1. The condition a+r-2<q retains all these targets and all incoming sources, so the actual quotient projection is an isomorphism on that page. This is a deduction from the tower used in BHS Theorem A.8 and Corollary A.11, not a separately numbered safe-range theorem in that paper. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7; pages local PDF p. 16; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

blocks.label: sem:Literature:vanishing-and-degeneration
blocks.title: Vanishing windows and inherited degeneration
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8 and Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $r\ge2$, one has $E_r^{s,t,w}(
u X)=0$ when $t<w$. For $q>0$, one has $E_r^{s,t,w}(
u X/\lambda^q)=0$ when $t-w<0$ or $q\le t-w$. If the classical Adams spectral sequence of $X$ degenerates at $N$, then the synthetic Adams spectral sequence of $
u X$ degenerates at $N$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.finite_quotient_vanishing
lean.code:
public theorem finite_quotient_vanishing :
  ∀ (X : ClassicalObject) (n : ℕ), 0 < n →
    ∀ (r : ℤ), 2 ≤ r → ∀ (s t w : ℤ), (t-w < 0 ∨ (n : ℤ) ≤ t-w) →
      IsZero ((model.family.quotient (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) n).Page r (s,t,w)) := by
  intro X n hn r hr s t w hout
  let E := (model.family.quotient (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) n).sequence
  let D := E.ssData (s,t,w)
  have hstrip : ¬ (0 ≤ t-w ∧ t-w < n) := by omega
  have hzero2 : IsZero (E.Page 2 (s,t,w)) := by
    apply (finite_quotient_component X n hn s t w).isZero_iff.mpr
    change IsZero (if 0 ≤ t-w ∧ t-w < n then
      (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page 2 (s,t) else ModuleCat.of ℤ PUnit)
    rw [if_neg hstrip]
    exact ModuleCat.isZero_of_subsingleton _
  have hfirst : E.r₀ = 2 :=
    (model.family.quotient (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) n).firstPage
  have hzero0 : IsZero (D.page (↑(0 : ℕ))) := by
    simpa only [D, Page, hfirst, sub_self, Int.toNat_zero] using hzero2
  have hBZ : D.B (↑(0 : ℕ)) = D.Z (↑(0 : ℕ)) :=
    D.eq_of_page_isZero _ hzero0
  change IsZero (D.page ↑(r-E.r₀).toNat)
  apply D.page_isZero_of_eq
  apply le_antisymm (D.B_le_Z _)
  calc
    D.Z ↑(r-E.r₀).toNat ≤ D.Z (↑(0 : ℕ)) := D.Z_anti (by exact bot_le)
    _ = D.B (↑(0 : ℕ)) := hBZ.symm
    _ ≤ D.B ↑(r-E.r₀).toNat := D.B_mono (by exact bot_le)

      IsZero ((model.family.quotient (model.nu.functor.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) n).Page r (s,t,w))

comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Partial source correspondence. No strong-convergence conclusion is asserted by degeneration alone. The displayed mathematical assertion is sourced for N>=2. The bound Lean degeneration interface quantifies every integer N; since DegeneratesAt asks for every differential r>=N, the N<2 portion additionally requires a below-first-page normalization for the actual synthetic family. BHS Theorem A.8 does not provide that project-specific portion. The canonical classical construction does set r<2 differentials to zero in Internal/Source/AdamsSequence.lean:207, but no matching synthetic-family normalization was found in this research. This is an unverified scope endpoint, not a verified counterexample or authorization to edit an interface. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9(1) and A.11(1),(3); the extension to $N<2$ remains unverified.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:cycle-quotients
blocks.title: Classical cycles, boundaries, and common permanent representatives
blocks.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{LWX126}, Notation 3.10.)\par{}

Let $Z_r^{s,t}(X)$ and $B_r^{s,t}(X)$ be the classical cycle and boundary subgroups of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$, and let $Z_\infty=\bigcap_r Z_r$. A classical permanent representative is an element of $Z_\infty$; zero is allowed. The cycle and permanent quotients are the corresponding subquotients of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:infinite-nu-window
blocks.title: The infinite page of nu X and its labels
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family,
\[E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong
\begin{cases}Z_\infty^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X),&w\le t,\\0,&t<w.\end{cases}\]
This is a linear isomorphism carrying the infinite representative of an $E_2$ label to its permanent-cycle quotient class.

deps.label: frontier:Literature:15195fec1630

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Proposition 3.11; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Corollary A.9, and [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Proposition 3.11.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:infinite-finite-window
blocks.title: The infinite page of a finite lambda quotient
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $q>0$,
\[E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)\cong
\begin{cases}Z_{q-t+w}^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X),&0\le t-w<q,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
This is a linear isomorphism compatible with labels and the quotient projection.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:infinite-shift
blocks.title: Shift comparison and naturality at infinity
blocks.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

For $k\ge0$, the shift $(0,-k)$ induces a filtered comparison and an $E_\infty$ comparison, natural in morphisms between objects in the chosen synthetic family. Composing with the map $\lambda^k$ gives the weight-lowering maps on the untruncated and finite-quotient infinite pages. At $k=0$ these maps are identities.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Project choice or construction. This is not an independently quoted literature theorem. The project proves naturality from the chosen filtered comparison, so source attribution should identify the construction. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Math. 232 (2023) [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Remark 3.14; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

blocks.label: sem:Literature:infinite-lambda
blocks.title: Lambda on infinite-page quotient coordinates
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

Under the infinite-page presentations, multiplication by $\lambda^k$ induces the natural map between classical cycle/boundary quotients. For $\nu X$, assume $w\le t$. For finite quotients, assume $k<q$ and $0\le t-w<q-k$; the source has length $q-k$ and weight $w$, and the target has length $q$ and weight $w-k$.

    infinityNuWindow X p (w-k) (by omega) (infinityLambda (.nu X) k p w x) =
      permanentQuotientMap model X (by omega) p (infinityNuWindow X p w hw x) := by

All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Remark 3.14; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

blocks.label: sem:Literature:infinite-restriction
blocks.title: Restriction between infinite-page windows
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

For $0<i\le j$ and $0\le t-w<i$, restriction $
u X/\lambda^j	o
u X/\lambda^i$ induces the natural map between the cycle/boundary quotients. Projection from $
u X$ to a positive-length finite quotient carries a permanent-cycle quotient class to its finite-cycle quotient class in the common strip.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.9(1)-(4), including its final surjectivity sentence; pages arXiv PDF pp. 72-73; published pp. 307-308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Remark 3.14; pages local PDF p. 17; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Corollary A.11 and its proof, and [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Remark 3.14.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:weight-epimorphisms
blocks.title: Weight maps are the actual lambda maps
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $w_1\le w_2\le t$, the weight map from $w_2$ to $w_1$ on $E_\infty(\nu X)$ is induced by $\lambda^{w_2-w_1}$. In quotient coordinates it preserves the permanent representative and enlarges the boundary subgroup. This map is an epimorphism. Thus multiplication by $\lambda^k$ on $E_\infty(\nu X)$ is an epimorphism whenever the source weight is at most $t$.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:cofiber-and-lift
blocks.title: Synthetic cofibers and full lifts of maps
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Lem. 4.23; \cite{BHS}, Lem. 9.15.)\par{}

For a classical cofiber triangle, its image under $\nu$ is a synthetic cofiber triangle if and only if its mod-two homology sequence is short exact. If $f$ has Adams tower filtration at least $k$, it has a synthetic lift whose composite with $\lambda^k$ is $\nu f$. A positive-filtration connecting map admits such a lift as the connecting arrow of the lifted triangle. Two full lifts may differ by $\lambda$ torsion.

Scope of the related interface family `literature-lift`. This note does not assert equivalence with a broader paper statement or mark any proof complete.


- **mathematical_purpose**: 任意经典映射及λ幂的全提升、ν余纤维与完整同调短正合等价、三角提升的λ-torsion条件。


Code provenance: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Exact original source blocks and migration history remain in `local-history/metadata/literature-sources.json`.

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS factors a map of filtration k. The interface uses the actual target Adams-tower lower-bound predicate and negative-target shifts; identifying that predicate with source Adams filtration is part of model recognition. The interface existentially chooses a connecting arrow and its distinguished triangle under positive filtration and homology exactness; its full-lift comparison is only modulo lambda torsion, as in AimPaper Remark 3.18. Specialization to mod-two homology and the project’s precise nu and coefficient functors; no finiteness, connectivity, or completeness premise is introduced. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Lemma 9.15 and its proof; pages 34–35; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Propositions 3.16–3.17; Remark 3.18; pages 18–19; Repository-frozen AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf [Pst](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.01804v3): Lemma 4.23; pages 43; arXiv:1803.01804v3, 10 November 2022

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [Pst](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-022-01173-2), Lemma 4.23, and [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Lemma 9.15; see [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Propositions 3.16--3.17 and Remark 3.18.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:normalized-cofiber
blocks.title: Normalized arrows and their actual cofiber comparison
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.20.)\par{}

For a triangle in the chosen classical object family, let its normalized arrows be obtained from synthetic lifts by shifting through their filtration exponents. The cofiber triangle of the first normalized arrow is distinguished and has a cofiber comparison. Call the normalized arrows compatible when the triangle formed by all three arrows is distinguished.

  ∀ T : TriangleData model.auxiliary,
    normalizedExponent model.classicalTower T.f +
      normalizedExponent model.classicalTower T.g + normalizedExponent model.classicalTower T.h = 1 →
    ∃ (f : model.nu.functor.obj (T.X.obj model.auxiliary) ⟶ model.nu.functor.obj (T.Y.obj model.auxiliary))
      (g : model.nu.functor.obj (T.Y.obj model.auxiliary) ⟶ model.nu.functor.obj (T.Z.obj model.auxiliary))
      (h : model.nu.functor.obj (T.Z.obj model.auxiliary) ⟶
        (shiftFunctor SyntheticSpectrum (1 : ℤ)).obj (model.nu.functor.obj (T.X.obj model.auxiliary))),
      Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang SyntheticSpectrum := by

lean.code:
public theorem nuCofiber_nu_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.nuMap = 1 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨_, _, b, hb, _⟩ := nu_detection
  have hmem : model.auxiliary.nuMap ∈ ModuleCat.subobjectModule _
      ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 3) := by
    change ∃ b, ((model.classicalTower.tower SphereSpectrum).filtration.F 1 3).arrow.hom b = _
    exact ⟨b, hb⟩
  simp only [AbstractAdamsTower.filtration, OrderIso.apply_symm_apply] at hmem
  obtain ⟨lift, hlift⟩ := hmem
  have hF : MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.nuMap 1 :=
    ⟨lift, hlift⟩
  change (if MapFiltrationAtLeast model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.nuMap 1 then 1 else 0) = 1
  exact if_pos hF

public theorem nuCofiber_nu_exponent :
  normalizedExponent model.classicalTower model.auxiliary.nuMap = 1

blocks.label: sem:Literature:finite-bockstein
blocks.title: Finite lifts and the Bockstein differential
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1) and Cor. A.11.)\par{}

Let $q>0$ and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$. The label $x$ reaches $E_{q+1}$ if and only if its first-quotient class lifts to $\nu X/\lambda^q$. Here reaching a page allows zero and boundaries. A suitable lift has Bockstein label representing $d_{q+1}x$ in bidegree $(s+q+1,t+q)$, where the Bockstein is the boundary of this quotient tower.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:differential-rigidity
blocks.title: Classical and synthetic differentials with common labels
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8(3).)\par{}

For $r\ge2$, the classical relation $d_r(x)=y$ is equivalent to the synthetic labeled relation $d_r(x)=\lambda^{r-1}y$. More generally,
\[d_r(\lambda^k x)=\lambda^{k+r-1}y.\]
After a shift $(0,a)$, both sides have weight $t+a-k$.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:bhs-applicability
blocks.title: The complete-source hypotheses for untruncated BHS
blocks.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{BHS}, Def. A.12.)\par{}

An object satisfies the complete-source hypotheses if countable products exist, the Milnor map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product of residual Adams-tower stages is invertible, and the tower admits a completion witness. Require also that the homotopy filtration is separated in every degree and that the canonical convergence identification holds for this tower.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:complete-permanent-lifts
blocks.title: Permanent lifts and filtration on a complete source
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1 and Cor. A.19.)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. A classical label has a common infinite-cycle representative if and only if it is the first-quotient image of an untruncated synthetic class. For a class of bidegree $(m,w)$ and $w-m\le s$, Adams filtration at least $s$ is equivalent to divisibility by $\lambda^{m+s-w}$ from weight $m+s$.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:complete-lifetime
blocks.title: Lifetime of a lift on a complete source
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2a).)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. Let $r\ge1$, and let a synthetic class $a$ have first-quotient label $x$. If $x$ has a common permanent representative and survives nontrivially to $E_{r+1}$, then $\lambda^{r-1}a\ne0$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.bhs_realization_lifetime
lean.code:
public theorem bhs_realization_lifetime :
  ∀ (X : ClassicalObject) (products : HasProductsOfShape ℕ Spectrum),
    BHSObjectApplicability model products (X.obj model.auxiliary) →
    ∀ (s t : ℤ) (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r →
    ∀ (x : (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page 2 (s,t))
      (a : BiHom (t-s) t (nuZero model X)),
    ClassicalPermanentCycle model X (s,t) x →
    SurvivesTo (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) (r+1) (s,t) x →
    quotientClass 1 a = firstLabel model X s t x → lambdaMultiply (r-1) a ≠ 0 := by
  sorry

blocks.label: sem:Literature:complete-detection
blocks.title: Detection and prescribed realization on a complete source
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2b),(3b).)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. The realization of a synthetic lift of a nonzero permanent label $x$ is detected by $x$ in the classical tower. Conversely, if a classical class $a$ is detected by such an $x$, there is a synthetic class with first-quotient label $x$ and realization $a$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.bhs_realization_prescribed_lift
lean.code:
public theorem bhs_realization_prescribed_lift :
  ∀ (X : ClassicalObject) (products : HasProductsOfShape ℕ Spectrum),
    BHSObjectApplicability model products (X.obj model.auxiliary) →
    ∀ (s t : ℤ) (x : (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)).Page 2 (s,t))
      (a : HomotopyGroup (t-s) (X.obj model.auxiliary)),
    NonzeroSurvival (model.classical.obj (X.obj model.auxiliary)) (s,t) x →
    ClassicalDetects (model.classicalConvergence X) (s,t) x a →
    ∃ b : BiHom (t-s) t (nuZero model X), quotientClass 1 b = firstLabel model X s t x ∧
      realizeNu X b = a := by
  sorry

blocks.label: sem:Literature:selected-lifts
blocks.title: The source-to-selected-model infinite-lift comparisons
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1 and Cor. A.19.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family, a classical label has a common infinite-cycle representative if and only if it is the first-quotient image of an untruncated class on $\nu X$. For a class of bidegree $(m,w)$ and $w-m\le s$, Adams filtration at least $s$ is equivalent to divisibility by $\lambda^{m+s-w}$ from weight $m+s$. A class on an object in the chosen synthetic family has zero realization if and only if some finite power of $\lambda$ annihilates it.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:selected-realization
blocks.title: The selected-model realization comparisons
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2)--(3).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical object family. A lift $a$ of a common permanent label $x$ surviving nontrivially to $E_{r+1}$ satisfies $\lambda^{r-1}a\ne0$ for $r\ge1$. If $x$ is a nonzero permanent label, it detects $\operatorname{Re}(a)$; each prescribed classical class detected by $x$ is the realization of such a lift. If a common infinite-cycle label $y$ is hit on page $r\ge2$, it has a lift annihilated by $\lambda^{r-1}$.

blocks.title: Exact tensor functors in the same synthetic category
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.2; \cite{May01}, TC1--TC2.)\par{}

Left and right tensoring by a synthetic object commute with suspension and preserve distinguished triangles. Equip both functors with these shift isomorphisms and exactness structures; together they define the May tensor context.

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{May01}, Lem. 4.6.)\par{}

For two cofiber triangles in the May tensor context, their tensor-product diagram admits May push-pull data and a signed boundary identity. If multiplication by two annihilates the relevant boundary image, the signed identity gives the corresponding unsigned identity.

Primary references: [May01](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/PAPERS/AddJan01.pdf): Axiom TC3; Lemma 4.6; pages 12–14; Author-hosted January 2001 preprint, 31 pages; numbered statements retain published numbering

blocks.label: sem:Literature:mapping-system
blocks.title: Mapping spectra and actual composition
blocks.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{Moss}, §1.)\par{}

Fix the closed tensor structure on the classical category and mapping spectra between objects in the chosen sphere family. Their Adams systems have composition pairings, common cycle products, units, and filtered abutment products. On spheres, composition agrees with sphere multiplication and its unit.

blocks.label: sem:Literature:moss-indeterminacy
blocks.title: The full Massey indeterminacy coset
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, §1.)\par{}

Let $r\ge3$ and let $a,b,c$ be composable labels in the mapping Adams system. If $x_0$ is a value of their page-$r$ Massey relation, then $x$ is another value if and only if $x-x_0$ belongs to the full Massey indeterminacy subgroup. All values have the page-$r$ Massey degree of $a,b,c$.

This is the ordinary triple Massey product in homology of the page-(r-1) differential, with r >= 3; it does not claim the distinct r = 2 cobar construction. Moss p.284 gives exactly this distinction and the quotient by both product summands. The project degree i+j+k-(r-1,r-2) equals Moss (p,q+1), where p=sum(s)-r+1 and q=sum(t)-r+1. Algebra 12 (1969), 533–568, author-hosted scan

blocks.label: sem:Literature:moss-convergence
blocks.title: Moss convergence with both crossing conditions
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Thm. 1.2.)\par{}

Let $W,X,Y,Z$ belong to the chosen sphere mapping family, and let $r\ge3$. Suppose the composable page-$r$ labels $a,b,c$ detect stable maps $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$, their adjacent page products vanish, and the corresponding stable composites vanish. Assume weak convergence of the two product towers and both of Moss's no-crossing conditions. There is a permanent member of the page-$r$ Massey relation detecting a stable class whose associated map belongs to the Toda relation of $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. The Massey relation includes a defining system on page $r-1$.

Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Moss's crossing convention differs from the paper's extension-crossing convention.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. Moss Theorem 1.2 assumes weak convergence of all five input/product Adams systems, not only the two product systems. For this fixed sphere mapping family, the separately bound global moss_weak_convergence statement supplies all five; the displayed StatementAt lists only the two product-tower premises. For each product degree u, put n=q in source condition (1.3): 0<=q<=u_1-r becomes 0<=q<u_1-(r-1), and an outgoing page m satisfies u_1<q+m (hence m>r). The source model is Boardman stable homotopy with Adams systems for a cohomology functor. Identification of the chosen project mapping system, the shifted stable maps and sign conventions remains a comparison obligation; this is not a theorem about arbitrary triangulated categories. Primary references: [Moss](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/download/pdf/PPN266833020_0115/LOG_0047.pdf): Section 1; Theorem (1.2) and conditions (1.3); pages 283–285; Original Math. Z. 115 (1970), 283–310; GDZ digitized journal scan LOG_0047 [BelmontKong2024](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.08689v2): Definitions 2.3–2.4; Theorem 4.10 and Assumptions 3.14, 3.17; pages 5, 12–13, 16–17; arXiv:2112.08689v2, 16 August 2024 (not a different published numbering)

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [Moss](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01129978), Theorem 1.2 and conditions (1.3), with the global weak-convergence hypothesis from Section 1.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:toda-relations
blocks.title: Toda witnesses and their indeterminacy
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{ChristensenFrankland2017}, Def. 3.1 and Lem. 3.4.)\par{}

A triple Toda witness consists of a distinguished cofiber triangle, null composites, an extension over the cofiber, and a boundary equation giving its value. A witness implies composability. For composable data, witnesses exist, and their values form a coset of the full Toda indeterminacy subgroup. In the synthetic sphere, use the fixed shift identifications.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The project uses the iterated-cofiber convention, with a fixed suspension identification for the synthetic TripleToda specialization. Existence uses exactness of a distinguished triangle. Full two-summand indeterminacy is retained; it is not replaced by a chosen bracket value. Primary references: [ChristensenFrankland2017](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1510.09216v3): Definition 3.1, Lemmas 3.4–3.5 and 5.12; pages 8, 11, 21; arXiv:1510.09216v3, 12 August 2017; closely matches AGT 17 (2017), 2687–2735 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [ChristensenFrankland2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.09216v3), Definition 3.1 and Lemma 3.4; used in [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), proof of Lemma 7.16.)

blocks.label: sem:Literature:toda-functoriality
blocks.title: Naturality, juggling, suspension, and tensoring for Toda relations
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{ChristensenFrankland2017}, Lem. 3.5 and Lem. 5.12.)\par{}

Pre- and postcomposition carry Toda witnesses to the corresponding witnesses, and factors can be absorbed into the first and last entries. Juggling, shuffle, and suspension preserve the cofiber relations. A compatible functor sends a witness to a witness. Tensoring on either side does the same when equipped with exactness and shift compatibility.

comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The fixed h-zero choice is normalized by the first-quotient label and lambda[h-zero]=2, as in AimPaper Example 5.8(4). BHS Proposition A.20 gives a complete low synthetic ring presentation, with relation (0) h-zero eta=0 and relation (9) tau h-zero=2. In stem two, the presentation forces pi_(2,3) to be generated by tau eta^2 (the h-zero factors vanish), so h-zero annihilates every element there. This last assertion is a derived low-degree consequence, not a verbatim statement of AimPaper Lemma 7.16. The project must still identify its selected constants with these normalized low generators. Primary references: [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Remark 9.5; Theorem A.8; Corollary A.9(1); Notation A.10, Corollary A.11; Proposition A.20, relations (0), (9), and Remark A.22; pages 32, 72–73, 78–79; published Acta page mapping supplied in bhs_pages/proposals.json; arXiv:1910.14116v3, as independently retrieved by the BHS audit worker

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Example 5.8(4), and [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Proposition A.20, relations (0) and (9).)

Source verification (2026-10-18): Partial source correspondence. Toda Corollary 3.7 gives the uniform classical order-two symmetric-bracket law. Baues--Muro Definition 1.2, relation (T6), and Theorem 1.3 supply the connective-ring-spectrum version with the image of the stable Hopf element. To apply it in the synthetic category, one uses the canonical stable enrichment (or the corresponding square-zero mapping module) and identifies that Hopf element in pi_(1,0) with lambda^2 eta using BHS Proposition A.20. AimPaper proof of Lemma 7.16 uses the displayed synthetic formula for theta-five. The bound Lean statement is broader: every theta in pi_(62,64) killed by two, without a theta-five detection hypothesis. The cited uniform law explains this extension, but the canonical-enrichment and selected-Hopf-class comparison is an additional source-to-project obligation, not a quoted assertion of Lemma 7.16. Primary references: [Toda1962](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/toda.pdf): Corollary 3.7; pages 31 (right-hand page of PDF page 18); Composition Methods in Homotopy Groups of Spheres, original book scan [BauesMuro2009](https://idus.us.es/server/api/core/bitstreams/57be0e00-a434-4786-b7e3-83a7eeed4e7a/content): Definition 1.2, relation (T6), and Theorem 1.3; pages 3 in the author manuscript; Author manuscript arXiv:math/0612450v1, 15 December 2006; published Comm. Algebra 37 (2009), 56–82 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Remark 9.5; Theorem A.8; Corollary A.9(1); Notation A.10, Corollary A.11; Proposition A.20, relations (0), (9), and Remark A.22; pages 32, 72–73, 78–79; published Acta page mapping supplied in bhs_pages/proposals.json; arXiv:1910.14116v3, as independently retrieved by the BHS audit worker

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.4.)\par{}

For each $q>0$, equip $S^{0,0}/\lambda^q$ with a commutative algebra structure in the symmetric synthetic category whose unit is the quotient inclusion. Its multiplication and the sphere tensor comparison induce a bigraded product. Multiplication by a projected sphere class equals the sphere action.

    IsCommMonObj (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q) := by sorry

blocks.label: sem:Literature:first-quotient-products
blocks.title: The first quotient identifies products with Ext products
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Thm. 4.46 and Lem. 4.56.)\par{}

Under the first-quotient equivalence, multiplication of classes in bidegrees $(t-s,t)$ and $(t'-s',t')$ is the classical sphere $E_2$ product in bidegree $(s+s',t+t')$. The action of an untruncated sphere class on a first-quotient class agrees with the same product.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.quotientAlgebra_first_quotient
lean.code:
public theorem quotientAlgebra_first_quotient (s t s' t' : ℕ)
    (x : BiHom ((t : ℤ)-s) t (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) 1))
    (y : BiHom ((t' : ℤ)-s') t' (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) 1)) :
    KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model ((s+s' : ℕ) : ℤ) ((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)
      (homotopyRegrade (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]; omega)
        (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]) (quotientAlgebraProduct (quotientAlgebra 1 (by decide)) x y)) =
      (eqToHom (congrArg (model.classical.sphere.Page 2)
        (show ((s : ℤ),(t : ℤ)) + ((s' : ℤ),(t' : ℤ)) = (((s+s' : ℕ) : ℤ),((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)) by
          simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add])))
        (model.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t')
          (KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model s t x)
          (KIP126.Literature.sphereFirstQuotient model s' t' y)) := by
  sorry

blocks.label: sem:Literature:filtered-product-detection
blocks.title: Filtration and detection of actual products
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, §1; \cite{BHS}, Rem. 9.5.)\par{}

A sphere class of filtration at least $s$ acting on a class of filtration at least $s'$ gives a class of filtration at least $s+s'$. On each positive finite quotient, if the two classes are detected by specified $E_2$ labels, their action is detected by the product of those labels, with the corresponding degree identifications. The classical product of detected sphere classes is likewise detected by the product of their classical $E_2$ labels.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.classical_product_detection
lean.code:
public theorem classical_product_detection (s t s' t' : ℕ)
    (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t))
    (y : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s',t'))
    (a : HomotopyGroup (C := Spectrum) ((t : ℤ)-s) SphereSpectrum)
    (b : HomotopyGroup (C := Spectrum) ((t' : ℤ)-s') SphereSpectrum)
    (ha : ClassicalDetects (model.classicalConvergence .sphere) (s,t) x a)
    (hb : ClassicalDetects (model.classicalConvergence .sphere) (s',t') y b) :
    ClassicalDetects (model.classicalConvergence .sphere) ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ))
      ((eqToHom (congrArg (model.classical.sphere.Page 2)
        (show ((s : ℤ),(t : ℤ)) + ((s' : ℤ),(t' : ℤ)) = (((s+s' : ℕ) : ℤ),((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)) by
          simp only [Prod.mk_add_mk,Nat.cast_add])))
        (model.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t') x y))
      (eqToHom (congrArg (fun n : ℤ => Sphere (C := Spectrum) n)
        (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]; omega : ((t+t' : ℕ) : ℤ)-(s+s') =
          ((t : ℤ)-s)+((t' : ℤ)-s'))) ≫ classicalSphereProduct a b) := by
  sorry

(From \cite{Adams60}, Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.~45.)\par{}

Write $H_{i,j}=h_i h_j\in E_2^{2,2^i+2^j}(S^0)$ for the actual bilinear product of the fixed standard classes. Its degree is the sum of the two one-line bidegrees; no independent label is chosen.

comments.text:
Fixed upstream source versions: [KIPSource5aa845241533](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/5aa845241533b763c37a1d5fc70cce9708c4e68e), [KIPSourcebbac1fc05843](https://github.com/SII-MATH/Kervaire126/tree/bbac1fc05843bdf2d56057e6114a38839e939378). Interface scope notes are retained as native hgraph node comments; historical migration records are local archives.

Clauses 1--2 detailed source attribution: [MayThesis1964](https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~obenoist/textes/May.pdf), Appendix A, pp.~A.1--A.2, and Theorem II.7.9, pp.~II-7.6--II-7.7, checked directly in the original 1964 Princeton thesis. The chart on A.2 contains h0^2, h1^2, h0 h2, h2^2, h0 h3 and h3^2; its source/target gaps and the standard connectivity argument exclude differentials. Theorem II.7.9(13) identifies nu-star with the E-infinity survivor h2 h4; parts (2), (3), (9) identify the nonzero Hopf-map squares. The h0^2 case follows from the chart and grading, not a direct assertion of that theorem. Remarks II.7.2, p.~II-7.2, identifies multiplication by h0 on E-infinity with multiplication by two. The existing AimPaper key Maythesis denotes the distinct 1966 Journal of Algebra article; it is not the thesis containing these locators. Original scan: [May thesis](https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~obenoist/textes/May.pdf).

Clause 3 detailed source attribution: [MahowaldTangora](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(67)90023-7), Section 8, is the historical source; this locator is explicitly corroborated in [Browder](https://doi.org/10.2307/1970686), p.~178, immediately after Theorem 7.1. The original MT scan has not been retrieved, so no independently verified MT theorem number is asserted. A directly inspected independent original proof is [BMMS1986](https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~may/BOOKS/h_infty.pdf), Chapter VI, Proposition 1.18(ii), p.~183: [Bruner's chapter](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/BMMS7.pdf). The public declaration's historical name is retained; its fixed-model proof is pending.

Clauses 5--6 detailed source attribution: The directly checked computations are [IWX](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10240-023-00139-1), Lemma 5.10(1), p.~143, and Table 6, p.~222, row (34,2,18), giving motivic d3(h2 h5)=tau h1 d1; and Table 7, p.~225, row (38,2,20), giving d4(h3 h5)=h0 x. The classical passage uses Corollary 1.2 and its proof, p.~111. The authors' original classical data [IWXCharts](https://zenodo.org/records/6987157), Adams-classical-E3.csv, physical rows 115 and 135 including the header, explicitly records the same d3 and d4 with nonzero targets h1 d1 and h0 x (rows 111 and 130). The primary IWX recomputations, rather than an AimPaper report, supply the checked mathematical source. This does not silently rename the frozen declarations or discharge their source-to-fixed-model obligations.

Nonzero classical source and target are independently explicit in the authors' fixed original chart release [IWXCharts](https://zenodo.org/records/6987157), Adams-classical-E3.csv, physical rows 472 and 457 including the header. Nonzero survival requires a common permanent representative and nonzero E-infinity image. The four differentials quantify over actual E2 target labels and require nonzero page targets; no arbitrary label is substituted. HHR Theorem 1.1 does not specify a differential length or target. Mahowald Theorem 1', p.~249, including the nonboundary argument following Theorem 2, and HHR Theorem 1.1, p.~2, were checked directly. blocks.label: paper:3.1
blocks.title: Synthetic cofiber sequences and homology exactness
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.1.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L759}{Source text}.
                          
[{\cite{Pst} ([Lemma 4.23])}]
    Suppose that
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z$$
    is a cofiber sequence of spectra. Then
    $$\nu X\fto{\nu f}\nu Y\fto{\nu g} \nu Z$$
    is a cofiber sequence of ${\HF}$-synthetic spectra if and only if
    $$0\to {\HF}_*X\fto{{\HF}_*f} {\HF}_*Y\fto{{\HF}_*g} {\HF}_*Z\to 0$$
    is a short exact sequence.

blocks.label: paper:3.6
blocks.title: Synthetic Adams pages and differentials
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 3.6.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L799}{Source text}.
                          
[{\cite{BHS} ([Theorem A.8])}] 
    The synthetic Adams spectral sequence for $\nu X$
     $$\SynSS_2^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\Longrightarrow \pi_{t-s,w}(\nu X)$$
     has an $E_2$-page 
    $$\SynSS_2^{*,*,*}(\nu X) \cong E_2^{*,*}(X)\otimes \mathbb{F}_2[\lambda]$$
    with differentials
    $$d_r: \SynSS_r^{s,t,w}\to \SynSS_r^{s+r,t+r-1,w}.$$
    Here $E_2^{*,*}(X) \cong \Ext_A^{*,*}(X)$ is the classical Adams $E_2$-page of $X$. An element in $E_2^{s,t}(X)$ is viewed as having tridegree $(s, t, t)$ in $\SynSS_2^{s,t,t}(\nu X)$, and $\lambda$ is in tridegree $(0, 0, -1)$. Given a classical Adams differential $d_r^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=y$, the corresponding synthetic differential is $d_r(x)=\lambda^{r-1}y$, which is $\lambda$-linear, and all synthetic Adams differentials arise in this way.

blocks.label: paper:3.8
blocks.title: The Adams and $\lambda$-Bockstein spectral sequences
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 3.8.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L813}{Source text}.
                          
[{\cite{BHS} ([Theorem A.1])}]
    The synthetic Adams spectral sequence for $\nu X$ is isomorphic to the $\lambda$-Bockstein spectral sequence (with no sign difference because we are working over $\bF_2$ here). More specifically, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $E_2^{s,t}(X)\iso \pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X /\lambda)$.
        \item[(2)] If we have a classical Adams differential $d_rx=y$ for 
        $$x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)\iso \pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X /\lambda),$$
        then $x$ admits a lift to $\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^{r-1})$ whose image under the $\tau$-Bockstein
        $$\nu X/\lambda^{r-1}\to \Sus^{1,-r+1}\nu X/\lambda$$
        is equal to $d_r(x)$.
    \end{enumerate}

blocks.title: The synthetic Adams infinity page
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.11.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L841}{Source text}.
                          

    The $E_\infty$-page of the synthetic Adams spectral sequence for $\nu X$ is given by
    $$E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\iso\begin{cases}
        Z_\infty^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X) & \text{ if } t \ge w,\\
        0 & \text{ otherwise }.
    \end{cases}$$

All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. (From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.12.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L849}{Source text}.

        Z_{r-t+w}^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X) & \text{if } 0\le t-w < r,\\
        0 & \text{otherwise}.
    \end{cases}$$
