Source verification (2026-10-18): Original source text. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. blocks.label: paper:3.17
blocks.title: Synthetic lifts of distinguished triangles
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.17.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L929}{Source text}.
                          

    Suppose that we have a  distinguished triangle of spectra
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z\fto{h} \Sus X$$
    with $\AF(h)>0$, and consequently a short exact sequence on $\HF$-homology
    $$0\to H_*X\fto{H_*f} H_*Y\fto{H_*g} H_*Z\to 0.$$
    Then there exists a distinguished triangle of synthetic spectra
    $$\nu X\fto{\nu f}\nu Y\fto{\nu g} \nu Z\fto{\Sus^{0,-1}\hat h} \Sus^{0,-1}\nu \Sus X=\Sus^{1,0}\nu X$$
    such that $\nu h=\lambda \hat h$.

blocks.title: Distinguished triangles with filtration shifts
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.20.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L965}{Source text}.
                          
Suppose that we have a distinguished triangle of spectra
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z\fto{h} \Sus X$$
    such that $e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1$. Then we have a distinguished triangle of synthetic spectra
    $$\nu X\fto{\hat f} \Sus^{0,-e(f)}\nu Y\fto{\hat g} \Sus^{0,-e(f)-e(g)}\nu Z\fto{\hat h} \Sus^{0,-1}\nu \Sus X$$
    (For simplicity we often omit the suspensions before maps but keep the suspensions before spectra.)

  j2 : vertex ⟶ T.Y ⊗ U.Y
  j3 : vertex ⟶ T.Z ⊗ U.X
  square : j1 ≫ (T.f ▷ U.Z) = j2 ≫ (T.Y ◁ U.g)

  boundary : letI := B.leftShift; letI := B.rightShift
    letI := B.leftExact; letI := B.rightExact
    j1 ≫ (U.map (tensorLeft T.X)).h = -(j3 ≫ (T.map (tensorRight U.X)).h)

blocks.title: The theta-five criterion

blocks.label: paper:7.3
blocks.title: A synthetic criterion for the survival of $h_6^2$
blocks.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 7.3.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2117}{Source text}.
                          
[Barratt--Jones--Mahowald, Burklund--Xu] 
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(1)]
 \item[(2)]    The element $h_6^2$ survives to the $E_{r+3}$-page of the classical Adams spectral sequence if and only if for some $\theta_5$, 
 $$\lambda \eta \theta_5^2 = 0 \ \text{in} \ \pi_{125,125+4} S^{0,0}/\lambda^{r+1}.$$
 \item[(3)]   In particular, $h_6^2$ is a permanent cycle in the classical Adams spectral sequence if and only if for some $\theta_5$,
 $$\lambda \eta \theta_5^2 = 0 \ \text{in} \ \pi_{125,125+4} S^{0,0}.$$ 
 \end{enumerate}
                        


\par The fixed-choice interfaces use the distinguished $\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}$ and a positive finite-page parameter. The normalized criterion at every admissible theta choice, including the zero-parameter case, is stated in \ref{sem:Main:any-choice-criterion}.

The bound Literature interfaces give the BX criterion only for the distinguished theta-five. comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The canonical nu-E Adams resolution can be tensored with C-tau^q. Its polynomial E1 terms truncate to exponents 0,...,q-1; the d1 calculation then gives the stated E2 strip. At weight exponent a=t-w, passing to page r inspects outgoing d_i for i<=r-1 whose target exponent is a+i-1. The condition a+r-2<q retains all these targets and all incoming sources, so the actual quotient projection is an isomorphism on that page. This is a deduction from the tower used in BHS Theorem A.8 and Corollary A.11, not a separately numbered safe-range theorem in that paper. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Corollary A.11(1)-(3) and its proof; Notation A.10; pages arXiv PDF p. 73; published p. 308; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7; pages local PDF p. 16; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Theorem A.8, Notation A.10 and Corollary A.11; grading as in [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Remark 3.7.)

comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. Put a=t-w. In the polynomial-lambda spectral sequence of BHS Theorem A.8, an incoming classical d_i has a source label with lambda exponent a-i+1. All incoming differentials contributing before page r have 2<=i<=r-1, so they all occur once a>=r-2. Outgoing cycles agree under localization. Thus the localization map is an isomorphism for a>=r-2, including the boundary case; this is a derived range, not the literal range printed in Corollary A.9(4). The inverse, E2 normalization, lambda square and differential square are obtained from this same localization map, rather than from unrelated choices of isomorphism. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The fixed h-zero choice is normalized by the first-quotient label and lambda[h-zero]=2, as in AimPaper Example 5.8(4). BHS Proposition A.20 gives a complete low synthetic ring presentation, with relation (0) h-zero eta=0 and relation (9) tau h-zero=2. In stem two, the presentation forces pi_(2,3) to be generated by tau eta^2 (the h-zero factors vanish), so h-zero annihilates every element there. This last assertion is a derived low-degree consequence, not a verbatim statement of AimPaper Lemma 7.16. The project must still identify its selected constants with these normalized low generators. Primary references: [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Remark 9.5; Theorem A.8; Corollary A.9(1); Notation A.10, Corollary A.11; Proposition A.20, relations (0), (9), and Remark A.22; pages 32, 72–73, 78–79; published Acta page mapping supplied in bhs_pages/proposals.json; arXiv:1910.14116v3, as independently retrieved by the BHS audit worker

blocks.title: Detection of the finite-quotient action
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Sec. 1; \cite{BHS}, Remark 9.5.)\par{}

Let $q>0$ and $s,t,s^{\prime},t^{\prime},k,l\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S^0)$ detects $a\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}S^{0,0}$ under the synthetic comparison, and the projected label of $y\in E_2^{s^{\prime},t^{\prime}}(S^0)$ detects $b\in\pi_{t^{\prime}-s^{\prime},t^{\prime}-l}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^q)$. Then the projected label of $xy$ detects $a\cdot b$ in tridegree $(s+s^{\prime},t+t^{\prime},t+t^{\prime}-k-l)$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.finite_action
lean.code:
public theorem finite_action (q : ℕ) (hq : 0 < q) (s t s' t' k l : ℕ)
    (x : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s,t))
    (y : model.classical.sphere.Page 2 (s',t'))
    (a : BiHom ((t : ℤ)-s) ((t : ℤ)-k) (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum))
    (b : BiHom ((t' : ℤ)-s') ((t' : ℤ)-l) (XModLambdaN (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q))
    (ha : Detects (model.convergence .sphere) (s,t,(t : ℤ)-k) (model.comparison.sphereE2 s t k x) a)
    (hb : Detects (model.convergence (.quotient q .sphere)) (s',t',(t' : ℤ)-l)
      ((model.family.quotientProjection (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q).pageMap 2
        (s',t',(t' : ℤ)-l) (model.comparison.sphereE2 s' t' l y)) b) :
    Detects (model.convergence (.quotient q .sphere))
      ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ)-(k+l : ℕ))
      ((model.family.quotientProjection (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum) q).pageMap 2
        ((s+s' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ),(t+t' : ℕ)-(k+l : ℕ))
        (model.comparison.sphereE2 (s+s') (t+t') (k+l)
          (by simpa only [Nat.cast_add, Prod.mk_add_mk] using
            model.sphereAlgebra.product (s,t) (s',t') x y)))
      (homotopyRegrade (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]; omega)
        (by simp only [Nat.cast_add]; omega) (sphereAction a b)) := by
  sorry

blocks.title: Filtration of the sphere action
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Sec. 1; \cite{BHS}, Remark 9.5.)\par{}

Let $X$ lie in the chosen synthetic object family. For integers $m,w,m^{\prime},w^{\prime},s,s^{\prime}$, take $a\in\pi_{m,w}S^{0,0}$ and $b\in\pi_{m^{\prime},w^{\prime}}X$. If $a$ has Adams filtration at least $s$ and $b$ has filtration at least $s^{\prime}$, then $a\cdot b$ has filtration at least $s+s^{\prime}$.

lean.name: KIP126.Literature.Standard.action_filtration
lean.code:
public theorem action_filtration (X : SyntheticObject) (m w m' w' s s' : ℤ)
    (a : BiHom m w (S_0_0 : SyntheticSpectrum))
    (b : BiHom m' w' (X.obj model.nu model.auxiliary))
    (ha : FiltrationAtLeast model.syntheticTower s a)
    (hb : FiltrationAtLeast model.syntheticTower s' b) :
    FiltrationAtLeast model.syntheticTower (s+s') (sphereAction a b) := by
  sorry

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1a)--(1b).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$. The label $x$ reaches $E_{q+1}$ if and only if there is $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ whose restriction to $\nu X/\lambda$ is the first-quotient class of $x$. Reaching a page permits zero and boundaries.

blocks.title: Infinite representatives in a finite window
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, $0\le t-w<q$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ and $z\in E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$. The projected weight-$w$ label of $x$ represents $z$ if and only if $x\in Z_{q-t+w}^{s,t}(X)$ and the finite-window image of $z$ is the class of $x$ modulo $B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X)$.

comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. BHS Corollary A.9 gives the untruncated E-infinity subquotient, and Corollary A.11 gives the finite quotient. All formula indices transform by s-omega=t-w. The finite formula holds for q>=1 in BHS, while AimPaper Proposition 3.12 explicitly states q>=2. Additive equivalences are viewed as Z-linear without a change of scalar structure. Matching a specific E2 representative to its quotient class requires the canonical label-compatible presentation, not an arbitrary abstract isomorphism. Zero labels are permitted in subgroup and quotient statements. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. blocks.title: Order-two classes and Toda brackets
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Toda1962}, Cor. 3.7; \cite{LWX126}, proof of Lem. 7.16.)\par{}

For every $\theta\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ with $2\theta=0$, one has $\lambda^2\eta\theta\in\langle2,\theta,2\rangle$. The first-quotient label of $[h_0]$ is $h_0$. If $a\in\pi_{62}S^0$ is annihilated by a power of two, then $2a=0$.

comments.author: blueprint-authoring
comments.title: Formal scope and provenance
comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Partial source correspondence. Toda Corollary 3.7 gives the uniform classical order-two symmetric-bracket law. Baues--Muro Definition 1.2, relation (T6), and Theorem 1.3 supply the connective-ring-spectrum version with the image of the stable Hopf element. To apply it in the synthetic category, one uses the canonical stable enrichment (or the corresponding square-zero mapping module) and identifies that Hopf element in pi_(1,0) with lambda^2 eta using BHS Proposition A.20. AimPaper proof of Lemma 7.16 uses the displayed synthetic formula for theta-five. The bound Lean statement is broader: every theta in pi_(62,64) killed by two, without a theta-five detection hypothesis. The cited uniform law explains this extension, but the canonical-enrichment and selected-Hopf-class comparison is an additional source-to-project obligation, not a quoted assertion of Lemma 7.16. Primary references: [Toda1962](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/toda.pdf): Corollary 3.7; pages 31 (right-hand page of PDF page 18); Composition Methods in Homotopy Groups of Spheres, original book scan [BauesMuro2009](https://idus.us.es/server/api/core/bitstreams/57be0e00-a434-4786-b7e3-83a7eeed4e7a/content): Definition 1.2, relation (T6), and Theorem 1.3; pages 3 in the author manuscript; Author manuscript arXiv:math/0612450v1, 15 December 2006; published Comm. Algebra 37 (2009), 56–82 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Remark 9.5; Theorem A.8; Corollary A.9(1); Notation A.10, Corollary A.11; Proposition A.20, relations (0), (9), and Remark A.22; pages 32, 72–73, 78–79; published Acta page mapping supplied in bhs_pages/proposals.json; arXiv:1910.14116v3, as independently retrieved by the BHS audit worker [IWX](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2001.04511v3): Corollary 1.3, Table 1, row k=62; pages [4, 6]

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [Toda1962](https://www.degruyterbrill.com/document/doi/10.1515/9781400882625/html), Corollary 3.7; [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Example 5.8(4) and proof of Lemma 7.16; and [IWX](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10240-023-00139-1), Corollary 1.3 and Table 1, row 62. The uniform synthetic comparison remains to be checked.)

blocks.title: Products on the first quotient
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Thm. 4.46.)\par{}

Let $s,t,s^{\prime},t^{\prime}\in\mathbb N$ and let $x,y$ be first-quotient classes in bidegrees $(t-s,t)$ and $(t^{\prime}-s^{\prime},t^{\prime})$. The first-quotient image of their algebra product equals the Ext product of their images, in bidegree $(s+s^{\prime},t+t^{\prime})$.

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.4.)\par{}

Let $q>0$, $x\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $y\in\pi_{k,l}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^q)$, with all four indices integral. Multiplication of the quotient image of $x$ by $y$ equals the sphere action $x\cdot y$.

blocks.title: Realization of lambda and the unit
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40.)\par{}

For all $m,w\in\mathbb Z$ and $k\in\mathbb N$, realization carries $\lambda^k:S^{m,w-k}\to S^{m,w}$ to the identity in sphere coordinates. At $(m,w)=(0,0)$, the sphere isomorphism agrees with the composite of the zero-shift identification, the inverse $\nu$--realization isomorphism, and the realization of the synthetic unit isomorphism.

blocks.title: Restriction between finite infinite-page windows
blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.14.)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $0<i\le j$, and $0\le t-w<i$. Under the infinite-page window equivalences, restriction $\nu X/\lambda^j\to\nu X/\lambda^i$ induces the natural map\[Z_{j-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}\longrightarrow Z_{i-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}.\]

blocks.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1c).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ reach $E_{q+1}$. There exists a lift $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ restricting to the first-quotient class of $x$ such that the Bockstein label of $a$ represents $d_{q+1}x\in E_{q+1}^{s+q+1,t+q}(X)$.

Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. This is the project-selected BX source choice, not a claim for every class with the same label. BX uses bidegree (stem, Adams filtration); the project uses (stem, weight), with weight = stem + filtration. Thus the source theta in degree (62,2) is displayed here in degree (62,64), and the source total boundary target is regraded to the project shift (1,-1). The finite statement retains r >= 1. Source-to-model identification and the registered Lean proof obligations remain separate from this citation check. Primary references: [BurklundXu](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.11869v3): Proposition 7.19 and its proof; Theorem 7.20 and its proof; pages 54; arXiv:2302.11869v3, 9 November 2024; accepted version [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879): Theorem 7.3, Remarks 7.4–7.5; Example 5.8(4); proof of Lemma 7.16; pages 42, 28, 49–50; Repository AimPaper/main.tex and AimPaper/2412.10879.pdf snapshot; no unstated version substitution

comments.text:
Source verification (2026-10-18): Source adaptation checked. The public shift isomorphism includes integer pages below 2; those pages are frozen to the first page by a project convention, not covered as extra pages in the cited paper. Write the BHS coordinates as (s,k,omega) and the project coordinates as (s,t,w). The translation is k=t-s and omega=w-(t-s); tau is renamed lambda. Hence s-omega=t-w, and the BHS differential degree (r,-1,1) becomes (r,r-1,0). This verifies the mathematical source and its stated regrading, not the outstanding Lean comparison with the fixed project model. Existing Lean proof and transitive-dependency status must remain unchanged. Spectral-sequence page and E-infinity subquotient statements here do not assert convergence to untruncated homotopy groups; BHS Convention A.5 allows an arbitrary spectrum for Theorem A.8 and Corollaries A.9/A.11. Primary references: [Pst](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1803.01804v3): Definition 4.6; Definition 4.27; pages arXiv PDF pp. 39, 45; published pp. 609, 618; arXiv:1803.01804v3, 10 November 2022; numbering also checked in Invent. Math. 232 (2023) [BHS](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.14116v3): Theorem A.8; Notation A.6; pages arXiv PDF pp. 71-72; published pp. 306-307; arXiv:1910.14116v3, 10 May 2022; checked against Acta Math. 231 (2023), 205-344 [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/html/2412.10879v2#S3): Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7; pages local PDF p. 16; arXiv:2412.10879v2, 22 February 2025; local AimPaper/main.tex and PDF also checked

Detailed source attribution: (Adapted from [Pst](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-022-01173-2), Definition 4.6, and [BHS](https://doi.org/10.4310/acta.2023.v231.n2.a1), Theorem A.8(2); grading as in [LWX126](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.10879), Theorem 3.6 and Remark 3.7.)
